_about: Government and the war cabinet (the grand campaign). Every nation has a form of government. The player's has a war cabinet of ministers he appoints and decrees he can carry, both paid for in political capital (the same that courts neutrals and signs trade agreements), and the cabinet's trust in him, which rises with ground won and jobs done and falls with ground lost and jobs ignored. Every few months the cabinet, or an ally, sets a directive: an optional job with a deadline and a reward. Computer nations keep a caretaker cabinet and no decrees, so none of this moves their wars. Rules in src/campaign/government.ts.

democracy.name: Parliamentary democracy
democracy.blurb: The cabinet answers to a parliament and a free press. It gives its confidence quickly and takes it back as fast: good news and bad both count for more.

oneparty.name: One-party state
oneparty.blurb: The party is the state, and the leader's word is its law: 1 more political capital a month. The cabinet's confidence moves slowly either way, and it takes a great deal to shake it.
oneparty.crisis: is purged after a plot against the leadership

authoritarian.name: Authoritarian government
authoritarian.blurb: A strong man, a regent or a king's ministers rule with the army behind them. The cabinet follows while the news is good.
authoritarian.crisis: is dismissed by the head of state

ministers.name: The organiser
ministers.minus: He fights the cabinet for every man: half a point less political capital a month

ministers.name: The reformer
ministers.minus: Depots are stripped for his experiments: replacements 5% slower

ministers.name: The industrialist
ministers.minus: His firms take their share: income down 2%

ministers.name: The planner
ministers.plus: Every factory is given a quota: income up 5%
ministers.minus: The army waits its turn: new corps cost 4% more

ministers.name: The merchant
ministers.minus: The cabinet distrusts his friends abroad: its trust falls 0.3 a month

ministers.name: The statesman
ministers.plus: He carries parliament, party or court with him: 1 more political capital a month
ministers.minus: Trade is beneath him: agreements pay 10% less

ministers.name: The taxman
ministers.minus: Nobody thanks him: the cabinet's trust falls 0.5 a month

ministers.name: The paymaster
ministers.plus: Wages, pensions and bread prices are kept steady: the cabinet's trust rises 0.5 a month, and a directive missed costs half the trust

steps.name: Peacetime economy
steps.text: Shops are full and factories work one shift.

steps.name: War economy
steps.text: Factories go over to war work: income up 6%. The shortages are felt: the cabinet's trust falls 0.5 a month, and holding the country to it takes half a point of political capital a month.

steps.name: Total mobilisation
steps.text: Everything for the front: income up 12%. The country is driven hard: the cabinet's trust falls 1.2 a month, and holding the country to it takes 1.5 political capital a month.

steps.name: Volunteers and reservists
steps.text: The army is fed from the trained classes.

steps.name: General conscription
steps.text: Every fit man is called: replacements 20% faster, and 15% more men come of age for the army each month. Workers leave the benches: income down 2%.

steps.name: The last levy
steps.text: Boys and old men are called up: replacements 45% faster, and 40% more men reach the army each month. Income down 6%, and the cabinet's trust falls 0.5 a month.

notes.forms: 'capital' is political capital a month the form adds to the nation's own; 'swing' multiplies every gain and loss of trust; 'start' is the trust a cabinet begins with; at or under 'fallsAt' for 'trust.crisisMonths' months running the cabinet falls.
notes.capital: Political capital is the nation's own (diplomacy.json: what it earns a month and the most it can hold). Under 'lowTrust' the cabinet doubts the player: it withholds 'lowShare' of the political capital he would earn each month and 'lowIncome' of the treasury's income; at 'highTrust' or over it adds 'highAdd'. A decree that costs capital to keep ('capital' below zero in its effects) lapses a step when there is none left to pay for it.
notes.trust: Each month trust moves 'drift' of the way back toward 'rest', then by the month's news: 'province' for each province gained, 'home' for each home province lost, 'win' and 'defeat' for each battle, 'capitalTaken' for an enemy capital, 'debt' while the treasury is in debt, 'ringed' while the capital is under siege. No single cause moves it more than 'cap' in a month.
notes.appoint: 'cost' in political capital to put a minister in a seat ('costMinor' for a country that is not a great power), and 'wait' months before that seat can change again. The player's country opens its campaign with at least 'start' political capital.
notes.ministers: Each has a seat ('*' for any), a gain and a price. 'effects' multiply income, drafts (replacements), cost (new corps), research, trade and men (the class that comes of age each month, manpower.json), or add to capital and trust each month; 'missed' multiplies the trust a missed directive costs. What ministers and decrees add to trust or take from it is felt in full under every form of government.
notes.tracks: Decrees in steps. Each step replaces the one before. 'needs': 'war' at war; 'long' at war for 'needs.longMonths' months or with home ground lost; 'pressed' with 'needs.pressedHome' of the home country lost or 'needs.pressedMonths' months of war. Stepping down is free; the track cannot be raised again for 'decree.wait' months.
notes.directives: The first comes 'first' months into the player's campaign and another 'every' months after one ends ('retry' if nothing fitted). 'missed': trust lost for one ignored, 'base' and 'step' more for each ignored in a row, to 'most'; and for each ignored in a row the level trust settles at falls by 'rest', to 'restMost', until one is carried out: five in a row bring any cabinet down. One set aside costs 'aside' of that, and the next comes on the day it would have. take: months and rewards by the size of the town, money as a share of a month's income; the cabinet names a town only where the player's troops beside it (those two provinces off count half) outnumber its defenders, walls counted, by 'odds'; with none such it may name one down to 'least', as a hard one, with 'hard.months' more months and 'hard.reward' times the reward; a town it asked for and did not get is not named again for 'again' months unless there is no other. hold: a province of the player's own with troops in it, under siege or with 'odds' times its own troops standing against it next door; it counts only if the place was attacked or besieged while the order ran, and is withdrawn otherwise; 'siegeCapital' is the reward where the siege had already begun. raise: the army, in the field or forming, brought to 'grow' times its strength or by 'least' divisions, but never by more than the treasury and the months of income can pay for, and never twice running. trade: a country with nothing else to do is asked to sign a trade agreement. relief: an ally who has lost 'pressed' of its home asks for an attack on the enemy pressing it; one that has lost 'overrun' of it asks to be liberated; the reward is a corps of this kind.
